A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse-LaViDa study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite reflow and a small appendix addition.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, editing, understanding, grounding, and ablation results in Tables 1–8 and 10, with qualitative outputs in Figures 6 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds text-to-image throughput measurements across batch sizes in Table 11.

M1.justification: The sparse parameterization, register tokens, sampling procedures, step-causal attention mask, and training objective remain unchanged. Sections 3 and 7 and Algorithm 1 describe the same method.

E1.justification: Training-data coverage and the generation, editing, understanding, grounding, and qualitative tasks are retained. The added throughput experiment varies batch size within text-to-image generation without introducing a new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including Fast-dLLM on MathVista and the grounding baselines in Table 10. The new throughput experiment reuses LaViDa-O, already the principal text-to-image comparator.

E3.justification: New Section 8.4 and Table 11 introduce a text-to-image batch-size sweep over 1, 2, and 4, reporting throughput in images/minute. v1 has no such sweep. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 11 adds a sensitivity analysis testing whether the throughput advantage persists with larger batches. Existing caching/truncation, register-count, and training-strategy ablations, together with the qualitative case studies, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new throughput table continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 11 reports LaViDa-O/Sparse-LaViDa throughput of 2.82/5.52, 3.85/7.26, and 4.24/8.65 images/minute at batch sizes 1, 2, and 4. Batch 1 reexpresses the existing latencies; batches 2 and 4 add results under additional settings. Retained results are unchanged. Section 8.4 incorrectly credits LaViDa-O with outperforming baselines, whereas the table favors Sparse-LaViDa.

T1.justification: The diffusion definitions and equations, factorization assumptions, sparse-representation reasoning, and attention-mask construction are unchanged, including Equations 1–5 and the appendix derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about accelerating multimodal diffusion through truncation, registers, and step-causal attention while preserving generation quality and bidirectional capabilities.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and substantive limitations are retained, including limited acceleration for short outputs, inherited hallucinations, editing-related pixel shifts, and untested pretraining applicability. Section 9 continues onto another page without changing its content. The new throughput paragraph reports an outcome rather than a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, data filtering, training-resource disclosures, and Table 9 hyperparameters are unchanged. The new throughput section specifies evaluation batch sizes but adds no implementation, timing-procedure, hardware, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Shi et al., Simplified and Generalized Masked Diffusion for Discrete Data, as supporting prior work on masked diffusion foundations (v2 reference 54). Other works and the paper's research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short batch-size subsection, renumbers Additional Qualitative Comparisons from 8.4 to 8.5, and removes the author internship note. The existing narrative and section organization otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the small throughput Table 11 and reflows nearby appendix text, splitting the retained limitations around Figure 9 onto PDF page 19. Printed page numbers are removed. Existing figures and tables retain their content and overall design.

improvement.justification: Table 11 adds useful evidence that the throughput advantage persists at batch sizes 2 and 4, modestly strengthening the practical efficiency evaluation. This benefit is tempered by Section 8.4's incorrect attribution of the advantage to LaViDa-O and the fragmented limitations layout. The clearly labeled table still provides usable additional evidence; the core method and existing benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
